name: Snow Riff

band.style_feel: mid-tempo straight eighths, steady kick on 1 and 3 with open snare backbeat, sparse in the intro and fuller in the chorus
parts: Part A: intro - arpeggiated riff, drums and bass sparse
Part B: verse - same riff, light groove
Part C: chorus - full band, 16th-note strumming
Part D: bridge/lead - fuller band, guitar harmonies
Part E: outro - riff returns, winding down
band.tips: Sources give 104-108 BPM (drum transcription says 104); the riff is in G#m (Em shape, capo 4). Play the riff cleanly for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning and keep the pulse steady.

whammy.tuning: Standard (E A D G B E) with capo on fret 4 per tabs; not verified from a recording source
how: Keep the guitar in standard tuning (capo on fret 4 for the G#m riff); no DROPTUNE needed.
Turn the left knob to OCT UP.
In the outro, press WHAMMY on (rocker heel down, no sweeping) to add the octave layer; press again to switch off.
whammy.tips: Frusciante used an Electro-Harmonix POG for octaves on the outro, not a Whammy; OCT UP is only a rough substitute. I could not verify the tuning from a source, so treat standard + capo 4 as an assumption and skip the pedal if it sounds muddy.

memo: Red Hot Chili Peppers - Snow (Hey Oh): arpeggiated riff. Frusciante-style clean Strat tone, light compression, touch of grit and room.

name: Snow Chorus
memo: Snow (Hey Oh): louder sections / bridge. Crunchier amp with blues-style drive and a bit of delay.
